recipes.title: Freeman House Chai Concentrate (Copycat)
recipes.description: Ginger forward, demerara sweetened, restrained spice blend (no vanilla, star anise, fennel, or nutmeg).

items: 2 inch piece fresh ginger (about 30g), sliced and smashed
10 to 12 green cardamom pods, cracked open
1 tsp whole black peppercorns, lightly crushed
4 to 5 tbsp loose Assam CTC tea (or 5 Assam tea bags)
**Prep spices:** Crack cardamom pods, lightly crush peppercorns, slice ginger into 1/8 inch coins and smash, break cinnamon into pieces.
**Toast:** Dry toast cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, and peppercorns over medium heat 1 to 2 minutes until fragrant. Don't skip.
**Simmer:** Add water and ginger. Bring to a boil, then cover and gently simmer 25 to 30 minutes.
**Sweeten:** Stir in demerara sugar while hot until dissolved.
**Steep tea:** Off heat, add tea. Cover and steep exactly 5 minutes. Don't squeeze bags.
**Strain and store:** Strain, cool to room temp, bottle, refrigerate.

notes: Assam CTC tea gives the malty backbone. Fresh ginger is non-negotiable. Turbinado can sub for demerara.
Keeps 2 weeks refrigerated (best in 7 to 10 days). Freeze in ice cube trays up to 3 months.
Bitter? Tea over-steeped or boiled. Flat? Increase ginger 50%.
Dirty chai: add a shot of espresso. Stronger spice: simmer 40 minutes before adding tea. Less sweet: 2 to 3 tbsp sugar.

extras.title: Serving
extras.body: 1 part concentrate to 1 part milk (oat milk works great). Heat until steaming (don't boil) or pour over ice.

items: 4 to 5 black tea bags (or 3 tbsp loose Assam)

extras.title: Latte ratio
extras.body: 1 part concentrate to 2 parts oat milk (go 1:1.5 for stronger).

items: 2 to 3 tbsp evaporated milk (or half-and-half or coconut cream)
Brew tea mix in boiling water 5 minutes. Strain through fine mesh or cloth.
Stir in condensed milk while hot.
Pour over a tall glass of ice.
Top with evaporated milk. Don't stir, let it cascade.

extras.title: Street style move
extras.body: pour back and forth between cups to aerate before serving.

recipes.title: Hot Toddy

items: 4 to 6 oz hot water, just off boil (or lemon ginger honey tea)
Optional: cinnamon stick, 2 cloves, slice of fresh ginger
Honey in the mug first, dissolve with a splash of hot water.
Add lemon juice and whisky, top with remaining hot water.
Garnish with a lemon wheel and spices.

notes: Add whisky after steeping so you don't cook off the alcohol. Using lemon ginger honey tea as the base is an upgrade.

extras.title: Ratio (3-2-1)
extras.body: 3 parts prosecco, 2 parts bitter liqueur, 1 part soda water. Over ice with an orange slice.

extras.title: Liqueur options
extras.body: Aperol (sweeter, lower ABV), Campari (more bitter and boozy), Select (traditional Venetian, in between), Cynar or Contratto (adventurous).

recipes.title: Reed's Style Extra Strong Ginger Beer

items: 12 to 16 oz fresh ginger (3 to 4x a normal recipe)
Juice of 3 to 4 lemons or limes
1/4 cup ginger bug liquid OR 1/4 tsp champagne yeast
Grate or food process ginger (skin on). Boil in 4 cups water 15 to 20 minutes.
Off heat, add sugar, honey, and cayenne. Steep 1 to 2 hours (or overnight). Strain, pressing the pulp hard.
Add citrus juice and remaining 4 cups cold water. Cool to room temp.
Add ginger bug or champagne yeast.
Bottle in pressure-rated flip-top bottles, 1.5 inches headspace. Ferment 3 to 4 days at room temp, burping twice daily.
Refrigerate once very fizzy. Let it sit 3 to 5 days in the fridge before drinking.

extras.title: Safety
extras.body: This much sugar creates serious pressure. Burp bottles and refrigerate promptly.

ingredients.name: Ginger bug (5 to 7 days)
items: 2 to 3 inches fresh ginger, unpeeled, grated

steps.name: Ginger bug (5 to 7 days)
items: Combine in a jar, cover with cloth.
Each day add 1 tbsp grated ginger and 1 tbsp sugar, stir.
Ready when bubbly and yeasty smelling.
Feed weekly at room temp or every 2 weeks refrigerated.

steps.name: Ginger beer
items: Boil ginger in 4 cups water 10 to 15 minutes. Add sugar, steep 30 to 60 minutes.
Strain. Add lemon juice and remaining 4 cups cold water. Cool to room temp.
Stir in ginger bug liquid. Bottle with 2 inches headspace.
Ferment 2 to 4 days at room temp, burping daily. Refrigerate once fizzy. Drink within 2 to 3 weeks.

recipes.title: Rebekah Peppler's Hot Toddy
recipes.description: A minimalist hot toddy: any brown spirit or amaro with honey and boiling water in a pre-warmed mug, scented with lemon peel and optional spices.

items: 2 oz scotch, bourbon, rye, Irish whiskey, dark rum, cognac or amaro
3/4 oz light honey, such as acacia, or maple syrup (or 1 tsp Demerara sugar)
Cinnamon stick and whole star anise, to garnish (optional)
**Warm the mug:** Fill a 6-ounce heatproof mug or glass with boiling water and let it sit 1 minute, then pour it out.
**Build:** Add the spirit and honey, top with boiling water and stir until the honey dissolves.
**Garnish:** Add the lemon peel, plus a cinnamon stick and star anise if you like. Let it cool slightly before drinking.

notes: By Rebekah Peppler for NYT Cooking.
Compare with the lemon-juice Hot Toddy earlier in this book; this one uses only peel, so the spirit leads.

recipes.title: Coconut Hot Chocolate
recipes.description: Dairy-free hot chocolate made with coconut milk, cocoa, bittersweet chocolate and brown sugar, crowned with a glossy whipped meringue.

items: **Cocoa:** Whisk the cocoa into 1/3 cup boiling water.

**Hot chocolate:** In a saucepan, simmer the coconut milk, brown sugar and salt, stirring, until the sugar dissolves, about 2 minutes. Whisk in the hot cocoa and the chocolate until smooth, then stir in the vanilla.
**Meringue:** Beat the egg white on medium until foamy, about 1 minute. With the mixer running, add the superfine sugar a tablespoon at a time and beat until shiny soft peaks form, about 5 minutes.
**Serve:** Pour into mugs and dollop with the meringue.

notes: By Melissa Clark for NYT Cooking.

recipes.title: Fluffy Pancakes

items: 1 tbsp butter or oil for the pan
Whisk dry ingredients in one bowl, wet ingredients in another.
Pour wet into dry and stir just until no dry streaks remain. Lumps are fine.
Rest batter 5 minutes while the pan heats.
Heat nonstick skillet over medium-low, add butter.
Pour 1/4 cup batter per pancake. Cook until bubbles form and edges set (about 2.5 minutes).
Flip once, cook about 1.5 minutes more. Hold in a 200°F oven on a rack.

notes: Buttermilk swap: 1.25 cups buttermilk, reduce baking powder to 1 tsp and add 1/2 tsp baking soda.
Don't press pancakes after flipping. Medium-low heat is the move.

recipes.title: Buttermilk Cornbread Waffles (Johnny Cakes Inspired)
recipes.description: A riff on Jeni's discontinued Johnny Cakes flavor, with toasted oat crumble and lemony blueberry preserves.

items: Preheat waffle iron to medium-high. Oven to 200°F for holding.
Whisk dry ingredients. Separately whisk buttermilk, eggs, butter, vanilla.
Combine just until no flour streaks. Rest 10 minutes.
Crumble: melt butter in a skillet, add oats, sugar, salt. Toast 3 to 4 minutes until deep golden. Cool on a plate.
Warm preserves until loose, stir in lemon juice and salt. Don't cook it down.
Cook waffles (1/2 to 3/4 cup batter each) 4 to 5 minutes until deep golden. Hold on oven rack.
Plate: preserves, fresh blueberries, crumble, maple syrup. Pat of butter optional.

notes: Use fine cornmeal, not coarse polenta. Make crumble same day. Optional scoop of vanilla ice cream or crème fraîche.

recipes.title: McDonald's Fruit and Maple Oatmeal (Copycat)

items: 1 tbsp maple syrup (plus a tiny drop of maple extract, optional)
Cook oats with water and salt about 5 minutes until thick.
Stir in brown sugar, maple, and cream.

notes: Toss apples in a little lemon juice and a pinch of cinnamon for brightness.

recipes.title: Golden Diner Pancakes
recipes.description: Sam Yoo's tall, yeast-risen buttermilk pancakes from Golden Diner in Manhattan's Chinatown. They're cooked one per skillet for height, then drenched in maple-honey syrup and topped with berry compote and salted maple-honey butter.
recipes.yield: Makes 4 to 6 large pancakes (3 to 6 servings)

ingredients.name: Pancake batter
items: 2 1/4 tsp (7 grams) active dry yeast (one 1/4-ounce packet)
1/4 cup (60 grams) canola or other neutral oil

ingredients.name: Berry compote
items: 14 oz (400 grams) mixed berries, such as blueberries, raspberries and stemmed strawberries cut to the size of the small berries

**Pre-ferment:** Whisk the yeast with 1 cup of the flour in a small bowl. Warm the buttermilk with 1/4 cup (60 grams) water over medium-low, stirring often, until lukewarm (about 100°F), about 5 minutes. Whisk it into the flour until smooth, cover and let sit 1 hour.

**Maple-honey butter:** Whisk the softened butter, honey, maple syrup and salt until smooth. Keep at room temperature if using within a few hours, or refrigerate airtight up to 1 week (soften and rewhisk before serving).

**Maple-honey syrup:** In a small saucepan over medium-low, heat the butter, honey, maple syrup, soy sauce and salt, whisking, until the butter melts. Whisk in 1 1/2 tbsp water until emulsified, then keep warm on the lowest heat.

**Berry compote:** Toss the berries with the sugar and cornstarch. Heat a large, deep skillet over high until a drop of water sizzles away instantly. Add the berries and cook, stirring now and then, until the blueberries look ready to pop, about 2 minutes. Take off the heat.
**Oven:** Heat the oven to 350°F with a rack in the center, and set a wire rack inside a sheet pan on it.

**Batter:** Whisk the remaining 1 cup flour with the sugar, baking soda and salt. In a large bowl, whisk the eggs and oil, scrape in the pre-ferment, add the dry mix, and stir gently just until no dry spots remain. Lumps are fine.

**Cook:** Heat one or two 7- to 8-inch nonstick skillets over medium until very hot; don't grease them. Fill with batter about 1/3 inch deep, smoothing it to the edges. Cook until the bottom is crisp and golden, 2 to 4 minutes, lowering the heat if it browns too fast. Flip and cook 1 to 3 minutes more, tucking in the edges to dome the pancake.

**Finish in the oven:** Move each pancake to the rack in the oven until the center is cooked through, 2 to 5 minutes (check with a paring knife). Repeat with the remaining batter, reheating the pan between pancakes.
**Serve:** Set one or two hot pancakes on each plate and drench with the warm syrup right away. Spoon on the berry compote, add a scoop of maple-honey butter and zest the lemon over everything.

notes: Recipe from Sam Yoo, chef and an owner of Golden Diner, adapted by Genevieve Ko for NYT Cooking.
Nonstick pans work best because they need no grease. Extremely well-seasoned cast iron also works.
At the restaurant, the butter is shaped into a football-shaped quenelle with two spoons.

sources.label: NYT Cooking (Sam Yoo, adapted by Genevieve Ko)

recipes.title: Shakshuka With Feta
recipes.description: Eggs baked in a cumin, paprika and cayenne spiced tomato and red pepper sauce, with crumbled feta that turns into creamy nuggets in the oven.

items: 1 large onion, halved and thinly sliced
1 large red bell pepper, seeded and thinly sliced
1/8 tsp ground cayenne, or to taste
1 (28-ounce) can whole plum tomatoes with their juices, coarsely chopped
3/4 tsp kosher salt, plus more as needed
1/4 tsp black pepper, plus more as needed
**Soften:** Heat the oven to 375°F. Heat the oil in a large ovenproof skillet over medium-low. Cook the onion and bell pepper gently until very soft, about 20 minutes.
**Spice:** Add the garlic and cook until tender, 1 to 2 minutes, then stir in the cumin, paprika and cayenne and cook 1 minute.
**Sauce:** Add the tomatoes, 3/4 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp pepper, and simmer until thickened, about 10 minutes. Adjust the seasoning and stir in the feta.
**Eggs:** Gently crack the eggs over the sauce and season them with salt and pepper.
**Bake:** Bake until the eggs are just set, 7 to 10 minutes. Top with cilantro and serve with hot sauce.

notes: By Melissa Clark for NYT Cooking.
Serve with pita or challah for scooping. Good for breakfast, brunch or dinner.

recipes.title: Waffles
recipes.description: Melissa Clark's crisp, tangy yogurt waffles that come together in one bowl in about 35 minutes.

items: 6 tbsp unsalted butter, plus more for the waffle iron
**Butter:** Melt the butter on the stove or in the microwave and set aside.
**Batter:** Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder, salt and baking soda in a large bowl. In another bowl, whisk the yogurt, milk, melted butter and eggs. Fold the wet into the dry.
**Cook:** Heat the waffle iron and brush it lightly with butter. Cook about 1/2 cup batter per waffle until golden and crisp, buttering the iron between batches as needed.
**Serve:** Serve right away, or keep warm in a 200°F oven.

notes: By Melissa Clark for NYT Cooking.
No yogurt? Sour cream or buttermilk work, or use another 1 cup milk mixed with 1 tbsp lemon juice or vinegar.

recipes.title: Dutch Baby
recipes.description: Florence Fabricant's classic puffed oven pancake: a blender batter poured into sizzling butter and baked until tall and golden.

items: 1/2 cup whole milk, at room temperature
Syrup, preserves, confectioners' sugar or cinnamon sugar, for serving
**Batter:** Blend the eggs, flour, milk, sugar and nutmeg until very smooth (or whisk by hand).

**Bake:** Put the butter in a heavy 10-inch skillet and set it in the oven. As soon as it melts (don't let it burn), pour in the batter and bake 20 minutes, until puffed and golden. Lower the oven to 300°F and bake 5 minutes more.
**Serve:** Cut into wedges and serve at once with syrup, preserves, confectioners' sugar or cinnamon sugar.

notes: By Florence Fabricant for NYT Cooking.
Room-temperature eggs and milk help it puff.

recipes.title: Eggnog Overnight French Toast
recipes.description: A whole country loaf cut in a deep grid, soaked with an eggnog-style custard spiked with rum, then baked until golden and dusted with nutmeg and powdered sugar. A pull-apart holiday brunch.
recipes.time: 1 hr 10 min (plus 30 min to overnight soaking)

items: 1 (16-ounce) day-old plain country bread loaf, oblong or similar
1 tbsp dark rum, brandy or bourbon

**Cut the loaf:** Have a rimmed dish about 1 inch deep that fits the loaf snugly. Shave a very thin layer (about 1/16 inch) off the bottom. Cut 1 1/2-inch slices across the top, leaving about 1/2 inch uncut at the bottom, then turn the loaf and cut the other way to make a grid. Set it in the dish.

**Soak:** Whisk the eggs, sugar, cream, melted butter, rum, vanilla and salt. Pour slowly into the center of the loaf, gently opening the pieces so every crevice and the top get soaked. Rest 30 minutes at room temperature, or cover and refrigerate overnight.
**Heat:** Heat the oven to 350°F and line a baking sheet with parchment.
**Bake:** Spoon any pooled custard back over dry spots, move the loaf to the sheet and bake until deeply golden and the custard is set, about 1 hour.
**Serve:** Dust with nutmeg and confectioners' sugar and serve right away.

notes: By Jerrelle Guy for NYT Cooking.

recipes.title: Sugar Moon Espresso Cornflake Cookies (Copycat)
recipes.description: Sugar Moon's espresso salted caramel cornflake cookie: a chewy brown sugar espresso cookie piled with salted caramel cornflakes. The topping is made like caramel corn, with cornflakes swapped in for extreme crunch. The cornflakes go on top only; they aren't mixed into the dough.

ingredients.name: Chewy brown sugar espresso dough
items: 1 cup (2 sticks) unsalted butter, room temp
2 tbsp finely ground espresso (real grind, not instant)
**Caramel:** Heat the oven to 250°F and line a sheet pan with parchment. In a saucepan, melt butter, brown sugar, corn syrup and salt. Boil without stirring 3 minutes.
**Coat:** Off heat, stir in baking soda and vanilla (it will foam up). Pour over the cornflakes in a large bowl and fold gently until every flake is glossy.
**Bake the cornflakes:** Spread on the sheet pan and bake 30 minutes, stirring every 10 minutes, until glassy and dry. Cool completely, then break into clusters.

**Dough:** Cream butter and both sugars 3 minutes until fluffy. Beat in the egg, yolk and vanilla. Whisk the flour, baking soda, salt, ground espresso and espresso powder, then mix in until just combined.
**Rest:** Refrigerate the dough at least 1 hour (overnight is better for chew and flavor).
**Bake:** Heat the oven to 350°F. Scoop 2 oz balls 3 inches apart on parchment. Bake 9 minutes until the edges are just set.
**Top:** Pull the pan, pile a generous handful of caramel cornflakes on each cookie and press lightly. Return to the oven 2 to 3 minutes so the caramel softens and fuses to the cookie.
**Finish:** Sprinkle flaky salt immediately. Cool on the pan 10 minutes; centers should stay soft and chewy.

notes: Based on Sugar Moon's own description (Aug 14, 2021): "chewy brown sugar espresso cookie… topped with salted caramel cornflakes (caramel corn but substituted corn flakes for extreme crunch)."
All brown sugar (mostly dark) gives the chewy, crackly, toffee-colored base in the photo.
Make extra cornflakes. They keep 1 week airtight and are great over ice cream.

recipes.title: Bakery Cookie Skillet
recipes.description: For reheating a store-bought bakery cookie into a skillet dessert.

items: Place cookie in a small oven-safe skillet (6 inch cast iron ideal). Optionally preheat the empty skillet 1 minute for a toasted bottom.
Add a few pats of butter and extra chocolate chips. Drizzle 1 to 2 tsp milk or cream over the top.
Warm at 300 to 325°F for 5 to 8 minutes until edges crisp and center goes soft.
Optional: broil 30 to 60 seconds for crisp edges (skip for thin, crispy cookies).
Top with vanilla ice cream and a pinch of flaky salt. Serve from the hot skillet.

recipes.title: Soft and Chewy Oatmeal Chocolate Chip Cookies
recipes.description: Danielle's oatmeal chocolate chip cookies from Live Well Bake Often: packed with rolled oats and chocolate chips, soft and chewy, and easy to make.

items: 1 cup (125 grams) all-purpose flour, spooned and leveled
1/2 cup (100 grams) light brown sugar, packed
**Dry mix:** In a medium bowl, whisk the flour, cinnamon, baking soda and salt. Stir in the rolled oats and set aside.
**Cream:** In a stand mixer with the paddle (or with a hand mixer), beat the butter, brown sugar and granulated sugar 1 to 2 minutes, until well combined.
**Egg:** Mix in the egg and vanilla, scraping down the sides of the bowl as needed.
**Combine:** Add the dry ingredients and mix on low until just combined, then mix in the chocolate chips on low until evenly distributed.
**Chill:** Cover tightly and refrigerate at least 30 minutes.
**Heat:** Meanwhile, preheat the oven to 350°F (177°C). Line two large baking sheets with parchment or silicone mats.
**Scoop:** Use a 1.5 tbsp cookie scoop to portion the dough onto the sheets, leaving a little room between each. Gently press each ball to flatten slightly.
**Bake:** Bake 10 to 13 minutes, until the tops are set.
**Cool:** Cool on the baking sheet 5 to 10 minutes, then move to a wire rack to cool completely.

notes: Store in an airtight container on the counter for up to 1 week.
Use old-fashioned rolled oats for the chewiest texture. Quick oats work, but the texture won't be quite the same.
Only have salted butter? Cut the salt to a tiny pinch.
Make ahead: the dough keeps 2 to 3 days, covered tightly in the fridge. If it's too cold to scoop, let it sit 20 minutes at room temperature.
Freeze dough: scoop, roll and gently flatten the balls on a parchment-lined sheet, freeze, then store in a freezer bag up to 3 months. Bake from frozen, adding 1 to 2 minutes if needed.
Baked cookies freeze well up to 3 months. Thaw to room temperature before serving.

recipes.title: Pan de Muerto
recipes.description: Soft, buttery, orange-scented sweet bread for Día de Muertos (Nov 1–2), topped with crossed dough "bones" and a coat of sugar.

ingredients.name: Dough
items: 3 large eggs plus 2 yolks, room temp
1 tbsp orange blossom water (agua de azahar)
1/2 cup (113g) unsalted butter, softened and cubed

ingredients.name: Topping
items: 1/2 cup sugar, rubbed with a little orange zest
**Infuse:** Warm the milk with the anise seeds until steaming. Steep 10 minutes, strain, and cool to lukewarm (about 100°F).
**Mix:** In a stand mixer, combine flour, sugar, yeast, salt and orange zest. Add the milk, eggs, yolks and orange blossom water. Mix on low 5 minutes until a shaggy dough forms.
**Butter:** On medium, add butter a few cubes at a time. Knead 10 to 12 minutes until smooth, glossy and elastic. It will be soft and tacky, so resist adding much flour.
**First rise:** Cover and let rise somewhere warm 1.5 to 2 hours until doubled. (Or refrigerate overnight; cold dough is much easier to shape.)
**Divide:** Set aside about 1/5 of the dough (around 150g) for decorations. Split the rest in half and shape each into a tight, smooth ball. Place on a parchment-lined sheet and flatten slightly.
**Bones:** From the reserved dough, roll 2 small marbles for the skulls. Roll the rest into 4 ropes about as long as the loaves are wide. Press with spread fingers as you roll to make knobby "bones."
**Decorate:** Brush the loaves with egg wash. Lay 2 bones across each loaf in an X, then press a skull ball in the center. Brush again to glue everything down.
**Second rise:** Cover loosely and let rise 45 to 60 minutes until puffy. Preheat the oven to 350°F.
**Bake:** Brush gently with egg wash. Bake 30 to 35 minutes until deep golden and 190°F inside. Tent with foil around 20 minutes if browning fast.
**Finish:** Cool 10 minutes. Brush all over with melted butter and sprinkle heavily with orange sugar.

notes: No orange blossom water? Use 1 tsp vanilla plus extra orange zest.
Keeps 2 days wrapped at room temp. Refresh 5 minutes in a 300°F oven.
Serve with Mexican hot chocolate, champurrado, or a latte made with the Freeman House chai.

recipes.title: Latino Foodie Pan de Muerto
recipes.description: Art Rodriguez's pan de muerto from Latino Foodie: an anise and orange scented sweet bread made as six individual loaves, each crossed with dough bones, brushed with butter and finished with sugar.

ingredients.name: Dough
items: 1/2 cup (1 stick) unsalted butter, room temp
**Bloom:** In a medium glass bowl, whisk the milk, water and yeast. Let it activate in a warm spot until foamy, 5 to 10 minutes.
**Sponge:** Whisk in 1/2 cup of the flour. Rest uncovered until doubled in size, about 25 minutes.
**Cream:** In a stand mixer with the paddle, cream the butter and sugar on medium until fluffy, about 2 minutes.
**Eggs:** Beat in the eggs one at a time on medium until fully incorporated, about 1 minute.
**Add the sponge:** Switch to the dough hook, add the yeast mixture and mix on medium until combined, about 2 minutes.
**Flour:** On low, add the remaining flour about 1/2 cup at a time, scraping down the sides, until the dough pulls away from the bowl, about 5 minutes. It may stay a little tacky.
**Flavor:** Add the orange zest, anise seed and salt. Mix with the dough hook about 5 minutes more, until less tacky and the dough comes off the sides easily.
**First rise:** Knead briefly by hand into a ball. Place in a greased bowl, cover with plastic wrap and let double in a warm place, 1 1/2 to 2 hours.
**Divide:** Gently punch down the dough, turn it out onto a clean surface and divide into 6 equal pieces.

**Shape:** From one piece, cut off 3 small pieces (about 1 tbsp or 1/2 oz each) for the bones. Roll the large piece into a tight ball and set it on a baking sheet. Roll the small pieces into balls, then roll two of them into long, finger-like bones.
**Decorate:** Lightly brush the loaf with water. Lay the two bones over it in an X, poke down where they cross, and set the last small ball on top. Repeat with the remaining dough for 6 loaves.
**Second rise:** Cover with plastic wrap and let rise in a warm spot, about 45 minutes. Preheat the oven to 350°F for the last 15 minutes of proofing.
**Bake:** Bake until golden brown, 25 to 30 minutes, tenting with foil if they brown too fast. Let cool completely.
**Topping:** Melt the butter and let it cool. Brush it over the loaves, then sprinkle generously with sugar.

notes: Recipe and photo by Art Rodriguez for Latino Foodie.
Compared with the other Pan de Muerto in this book, this one leans on anise and orange zest instead of orange blossom water, and makes six smaller loaves.

recipes.title: Gingerbread Latte Cookies
recipes.description: Espresso-spiked gingerbread cookies made with both fresh and ground ginger, rolled in espresso sugar for crisp edges and soft, pillowy centers.

ingredients.name: Cookies
items: 1 tbsp (17 grams) finely grated fresh ginger
1/2 cup (107 grams) dark brown sugar, packed

**Spiced butter:** Melt the butter in a medium saucepan over medium. When it foams, take it off the heat and whisk in the espresso powder, fresh ginger, ground ginger, cinnamon, nutmeg and clove. Scrape into a mixing bowl and cool about 5 minutes.
**Batter:** Whisk in both sugars, the molasses and salt. Add the egg, vanilla and baking soda and whisk until smooth and the texture of thin pancake batter, about 2 minutes. Mix in the flour.
**Chill:** Cover and refrigerate at least 2 hours and up to 2 days.
**Heat:** Heat the oven to 375°F with racks in the upper and lower thirds. Line 2 baking sheets with parchment. Stir together the coating sugar, espresso powder and ginger.
**Shape:** Scoop 2 tbsp (1 oz) portions, roll into walnut-size balls and toss in the coating.
**Bake:** Space 2 inches apart and bake, rotating the sheets halfway, until spread slightly and craggy on top, about 10 minutes.
**Cool:** Cool on the sheets 3 minutes, then move to a rack. They flatten as they cool.

notes: By Vaughn Vreeland for NYT Cooking.
Keep airtight at room temperature 4 to 5 days.
Freeze portioned dough balls, then coat and bake from frozen for about 13 minutes.

recipes.title: Chocolate Soufflés
recipes.description: Four tall chocolate soufflés: a cocoa, coffee and bittersweet chocolate base lightened with glossy beaten egg whites.

items: Unsalted butter, at room temperature, for the ramekins
7 tbsp (87 grams) granulated sugar, plus more for sprinkling and the ramekins
2 tbsp Dutch-processed cocoa powder, sifted if lumpy
4 oz (113 grams) bittersweet chocolate (70 percent cacao), coarsely chopped
5 large egg whites, at room temperature

**Ramekins:** Heat the oven to 425°F with a rack in the center. Brush four 6-ounce ramekins with soft butter, using upward strokes up the sides all the way to the rim. Coat with sugar and tap out the excess.

**Base:** Bring about 1 inch of water to a simmer in a medium saucepan. In a heatproof bowl, whisk 3 tbsp (37 grams) of the sugar with 2 of the yolks until pale, light and thick, about 1 minute. Slowly whisk in the milk, then the coffee, then the flour and cocoa until smooth.

**Cook the base:** Set the bowl over the simmering water without touching it and whisk constantly until it's like thin pancake batter, faintly holds whisk marks and the foam has subsided, about 5 minutes. Remove from the heat.

**Chocolate:** Whisk in the chopped chocolate, let it sit a few minutes to melt, then whisk smooth. Whisk in the remaining yolk and the vanilla. Let cool slightly, but not completely or the chocolate will set.

**Whites:** In a clean metal or glass bowl (not plastic), beat the whites and salt on medium-low until frothy, about 20 seconds, then on medium-high until foamy and opaque, about 30 seconds. Stream in the remaining 4 tbsp (50 grams) sugar and beat just until dense, glossy and holding stiff peaks. Don't overbeat.
**Fold:** Quickly whisk a third of the whites into the chocolate base, then fold in the rest in 2 additions with a large spatula until almost streak-free.

**Fill:** Divide all the batter among the ramekins, filling them to the very top. Tap gently, then level each flush with the rim using an offset spatula or butter knife. Discard any small amount left over.

**Prep the tops:** Sprinkle the tops with a thin, even layer of sugar. Run your thumb around the inside rim of each ramekin to clear a ring of batter so they rise straight up. Wipe the rims and outsides clean.

**Bake:** Set the ramekins on a sheet pan, put them in the oven and immediately lower the heat to 375°F. Bake until risen, firm and springy on top with a slight wobble, 15 to 20 minutes. Serve immediately.

notes: By Claire Saffitz for NYT Cooking.
The keys: stable, glossy whites; working quickly; and thoroughly buttered ramekins so the batter can climb.

recipes.title: Conchas
recipes.description: Soft, brioche-style Mexican sweet buns with a crumbly sugar topping scored like a seashell. Choose vanilla, café con leche or cocoa.
recipes.time: 1 1/2 hr (plus 4 to 24 hr chilled rise and 1 1/2 to 2 hr proof)

ingredients.name: Dough
items: 4 cups (520 grams) all-purpose flour (or bread flour), plus more for dusting
3/4 cup (175 grams) whole milk, at room temperature
13 tbsp (185 grams) unsalted butter, diced and at room temperature, plus more for greasing

ingredients.name: Vanilla topping
ingredients.note: pick one topping; each covers all 15 buns
items: 1 1/2 cups (184 grams) all-purpose flour, plus more as needed

ingredients.name: Café con leche topping
items: 1 1/2 cups (184 grams) all-purpose flour, plus more as needed
2 tbsp instant espresso mixed with 2 tsp boiling water

ingredients.name: Cocoa topping
items: 1 1/3 cups (170 grams) all-purpose flour, plus more as needed
1/4 cup (22 grams) cocoa powder mixed with 3 tbsp boiling water

**Mix the dough:** In a stand mixer with the dough hook, whisk the flour, sugar, salt and yeast. Add the milk, eggs and vanilla and mix on the lowest speed about 20 seconds. Raise to medium-high and knead until the dough slaps the bowl and forms a smooth, elastic ball around the hook, 10 to 15 minutes. Stay close; the mixer will walk.
**Add the butter:** On low, add the butter in 3 or 4 additions, then knead on medium-high until the dough is very soft, silky and shiny and hugs the hook again, 8 to 12 minutes.
**Cold rise:** Move the dough to a buttered bowl. Stretch and fold: lift the dough and fold it over itself, rotate the bowl 90 degrees and repeat 3 more times. Cover and refrigerate 4 to 24 hours.

**Shape:** Line three 13-by-18-inch sheet pans with parchment. On a lightly floured counter, cut the dough into 15 pieces (about 76 grams each). Pat each flat, gather the edges into the center and pinch, then flip and roll under a cupped hand into a neat ball. Place 5 on each sheet.
**Topping:** Beat your chosen topping with the paddle on the lowest speed 20 to 30 seconds, then on medium until smooth and glossy, about 2 minutes.

**Top the buns:** Divide the topping into 15 portions (about 30 grams each). With wet hands, roll each into a ball and pat into a 3 1/2-inch round. Lay it over a bun and press lightly around the edge, stopping at least 1/4 inch above the parchment.
**Score:** Dip a concha mold or dinner knife in flour and press a shell pattern into the topping without cutting through to the dough.
**Proof:** Cover with kitchen towels and let rise in a warm, draft-free spot until noticeably puffed, 1 1/2 to 2 hours. They don't need to double.
**Bake:** Heat the oven to 375°F. Bake until golden and puffed, 20 to 22 minutes, baking the third sheet after the first two if needed.
**Rest:** Let rest a few minutes before serving.

notes: By Pati Jinich for NYT Cooking.
Bread flour gives taller, chewier and slightly less sweet buns.
To try several flavors, make a half or third of each topping and mix it by hand or with a hand mixer.
Best the day they're baked. Keep airtight up to 4 days.

recipes.title: Peach Cobbler
recipes.description: Juicy maple-spiced peaches under a biscuit topping with oats for crisp-like crunch. Works with fresh or frozen peaches year-round.

ingredients.name: Filling
items: Unsalted butter, at room temperature, for the pan
5 ripe but firm peaches, peeled, halved, cored and sliced, or 2 pounds frozen peaches, thawed and drained (about 4 cups)
**Heat:** Heat the oven to 350°F. Butter a cast-iron skillet or 9-inch square glass baking dish.

**Peaches:** In a medium saucepan over medium, combine the peaches, sugar, vanilla, cinnamon, nutmeg and salt. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the sugar dissolves and the peaches release juice, 3 to 4 minutes.
**Thicken:** Stir the maple syrup and cornstarch together, add to the peaches and cook, stirring, about 1 minute, until the liquid coats the back of a spoon. Take off the heat.

**Topping:** Mix the flour, oats, sugar, baking powder and salt in a large bowl. Grate in the frozen butter and rub it in with your hands until pea-size. Stir in 3/4 cup buttermilk a little at a time, adding more only as needed to bring it together.
**Assemble:** Pour the peaches into the pan. Drop scoops of the biscuit dough on top with a little space between them and sprinkle with turbinado sugar.
**Bake:** Bake until the top is golden and the peaches bubble, 45 to 50 minutes. Rest 5 to 10 minutes so the filling sets, then serve warm with ice cream and a little mint.

notes: By Millie Peartree for NYT Cooking.
Maple syrup stands in for the usual brown sugar for a lightly woody sweetness.
A handful of blueberries in the filling works well.

recipes.title: Warm Sweet Potato-Apple Pone
recipes.description: A spoonable, custardy Southern pone of grated sweet potato and apple with brown sugar and cinnamon, baked until golden at the edges and served warm with ice cream.

items: 2 tbsp melted unsalted butter, plus 2 tsp for greasing
1 medium sweet, crisp baking apple, such as Honeycrisp, Fuji or Gala
1 medium sweet potato, peeled and shredded (about 1 1/2 cups)
1/4 packed cup (55 grams) light brown sugar
**Heat:** Heat the oven to 375°F. Grease two 15-ounce au gratin pans or one 8-inch square baking dish with 2 tsp butter and set on a baking sheet.
**Apple:** Peel, core and shred the apple, then squeeze the shreds hard in a clean kitchen towel to remove excess water. Toss with the lemon juice in a large bowl.
**Mix:** Add the sweet potato, evaporated milk, brown sugar, flour, egg, vanilla, cinnamon, salt and the remaining 2 tbsp melted butter and stir until combined.
**Bake:** Divide between the au gratin pans and bake 30 to 35 minutes, or bake in the 8-inch dish 55 to 60 minutes, until slightly puffed, golden at the edges and no longer jiggly.
**Serve:** Cool 5 to 10 minutes and serve warm with vanilla ice cream.

notes: By Jerrelle Guy for NYT Cooking.

recipes.title: Strawberry Shortcake
recipes.description: Jane Grigson's classic: tender cream biscuits baked in buttered stacks, split while warm and filled with lightly crushed sugared strawberries and vanilla whipped cream.

ingredients.name: Berries
items: 1/2 cup sugar, or more to taste
**Macerate:** Hull the strawberries and halve or slice them. Gently crush about a quarter with a fork, mix with the rest and the 1/2 cup sugar (more if needed), cover and let sit about 30 minutes.

**Dough:** Sift the flour, 3 tbsp sugar, salt and baking powder into a large bowl. Rub in 3/4 cup softened butter as for pastry, then mix in 1 1/4 cups cream to a soft dough. Knead 1 minute on a lightly floured board and roll to about 1/2 inch thick. Cut an even number of 3-inch rounds, 2 per serving.

**Stack and bake:** Grease a baking sheet with a little of the remaining butter and set half the rounds on it. Melt the rest of the butter, brush a little on the rounds and top each with a second round. Bake until golden, 10 to 15 minutes.
**Split:** Pull the shortcakes apart and brush the insides with more melted butter.
**Cream:** Whip the remaining cream until it thickens, add the vanilla and whip just until thick.
**Assemble:** Set a bottom half on each plate, add cream and berries, cover with the top half, then add more berries and cream. Serve right away.

notes: From "Jane Grigson's Fruit Book," adapted by Nancy Harmon Jenkins for NYT Cooking.
Extra shortcakes freeze well; warm before using. They're also good toasted for breakfast.

sources.label: NYT Cooking (Jane Grigson, adapted by Nancy Harmon Jenkins)

recipes.title: Jamaican Brown Stew Oxtail (5 lb Practice Batch)
recipes.description: From the Oxtail Off competition prep. This is the home scale practice version. The full 28 lb competition recipe, shopping list, and day-of timeline live in the source chat.

ingredients.name: Braise and finish
items: 1/4 cup light brown sugar (for blackened sugar)
Onion, garlic, ginger, scallions (split into two halves)
1 whole scotch bonnet, thyme, allspice berries, bay leaves

ingredients.name: Spinners
items: 1 cup AP flour, 1 tsp salt, about 1/3 cup water
**Prep:** Rinse oxtail in cold water with a splash of vinegar or lime. Pat completely dry.
**Marinate:** Combine marinade, add oxtail, massage 5 minutes. Refrigerate 24 hours (48 preferred).
**Dry:** Pull oxtail, reserve marinade. Pat each piece dry.

**Blackened sugar:** Heat Dutch oven over high, add 1/4 cup brown sugar. Stir until nearly black and smoking (about 5 minutes). Carefully add 2 tbsp boiling water (it splatters). Stir into a dark syrup.
**Brown:** Add oxtail in 2 batches, coat in caramel, brown about 10 minutes per batch. Remove. Pour off all but 2 tbsp fat.
**First aromatic add:** Half the onion, garlic, ginger, scallions, plus whole scotch bonnet, half the thyme, allspice, bay leaves. Stir 5 minutes.
**Braise 1:** Return oxtail, juices, and reserved marinade. Add stock and water to almost submerge. Bare simmer, covered, about 1 hour (300°F oven or low stovetop).
**Second aromatic add:** Remaining aromatics, 2 tbsp white sugar, 1 tbsp browning.
**Braise 2:** About 1 more hour until meat is loose on the bone. Test at 45 minutes.
**Spinners (during braise 2):** Mix flour, salt, water into a firm dough. Knead 2 minutes, rest 30 minutes. Roll about 12 tapered 2 inch cylinders.
**Pull and strain:** Cool oxtail 15 minutes. Strain sauce through a fine mesh strainer, skim fat hard.
**Debone:** Pull meat in rustic chunks. Don't shred.
**Reduce:** Reduce sauce on medium-high until visibly thicker (about 15 minutes).
**Spinners in:** Simmer 18 to 22 minutes until cooked through with no chalky center.
**Finish:** Add butter beans and meat back to the sauce. Thicken with a flour slurry (flour whisked into hot braising liquid) about 15 minutes before serving.

extras.title: Key moves
extras.body: long marinade, blackened sugar, two-stage aromatics, strained glossy sauce, Pickapeppa and browning over Worcestershire.

extras.title: Competition Plating Options
extras.body:
Presentation ideas for the same braise, from the competition plating chat.

- **Pressed terrine (recommended):** Pack warm deboned meat into molds while still saturated with braising liquid. The gelatin sets it. Slice thick medallions, sear for bark, glaze with the reduction.
- **Short rib style:** Pull meat in the largest chunks possible. Stack 3 to 4 pieces vertically in a ring mold, glazing between layers. Height wins on competition plates.
- **Dumpling:** Wrap deboned meat in wonton wrappers or dumpling dough. Pan fry for a crispy bottom, steam the top. Serve in a shallow pool of reduced braising liquid.
- **Croquette:** Shred meat, bind with reduced braising liquid, form cylinders or balls, bread in panko or fine cornmeal, deep fry. Serve on scotch bonnet aioli or jus.

**Finishing touches**
- Scotch bonnet oil: blend scotch bonnet with neutral oil, then strain. Color and heat without chunks.
- Fresh thyme sprig across the top, thinly sliced scallion greens, a few whole pimento berries on the plate for aroma.

**Scaling note:** For big batches, braise in two pots rather than one giant one. Even consistency matters more than time saved.

recipes.title: Oxtail and Butter Beans
recipes.description: Jamaican-style oxtail braised until it falls off the bone in a rich, full-bodied gravy, finished with butter beans.

items: 2 Scotch bonnet peppers, pierced with a paring knife
2 tbsp chicken stock concentrate or 1 chicken bouillon cube
2 (15-ounce) cans butter beans, drained and rinsed
**Season:** Season the oxtails with the salt and pepper.

**Brown:** Heat the oil in a large pot over medium. Brown the oxtails in batches without crowding, scraping up the browned bits, about 3 minutes per side, until deeply crusted. Pour off all but about 2 tbsp oil and set the oxtails aside.

**Aromatics:** Add the scallions, onions, Worcestershire, curry powder, paprika, pimento and thyme and sauté until the onions are translucent, about 5 minutes. Add the Scotch bonnets, bouillon, tomato paste and browning and stir 1 minute. Add the garlic and ginger and cook 30 seconds.
**Braise:** Return the oxtails with enough liquid to cover them completely. Bring to a boil, then simmer, stirring occasionally, until tender, 2 to 3 hours.
**Beans:** Add the butter beans and heat through, about 5 minutes, or 10 to 15 for softer beans.
**Serve:** Remove the thyme, Scotch bonnets and any pimento seeds you see. Adjust the seasoning and serve hot with rice and peas and sweet plantains.

notes: By Millie Peartree for NYT Cooking.
A simpler one-pot cousin of the competition Jamaican Brown Stew Oxtail in this book.
The gravy is great sopped up with roti or naan, or over coconut rice and peas.

recipes.title: Golden Krust Jamaican Oxtail Stew
recipes.description: Golden Krust's oxtail stew: oxtails browned in nearly black caramelized sugar, braised with allspice, Scotch bonnet and thyme in two stages, then thickened with a flour slurry and ketchup and finished with butter beans.

items: 3 pounds oxtails, cut into segments by a butcher
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
3 tbsp fresh ginger, peeled and chopped
1 cup butter beans, or a 10 1/2-ounce can, rinsed and drained

**Blackened sugar:** Season the oxtails aggressively with salt and pepper. Heat a large Dutch oven over high, add the brown sugar and stir until it darkens and starts to smoke, about 6 minutes. When it's nearly black, add 2 tbsp boiling water (it will splatter) and stir.
**Brown:** Add the oxtails in batches, turning to coat in the blackened sugar, and cook until well browned. Set aside in a bowl and keep warm.
**First aromatics:** Add half the onions, garlic and ginger, the Scotch bonnet, thyme, allspice and a third of the scallions. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
**Braise 1:** Return the oxtails and their juices and add water to almost cover. Bring to a simmer, cover and cook about 1 hour, stirring occasionally.

**Braise 2:** Add the remaining onions, garlic and ginger, another third of the scallions, the white sugar, soy sauce and Worcestershire. Cook until the meat is yielding and loose on the bone, about 1 hour more.
**Thicken:** Ladle about 1 cup of the liquid into a bowl, stir in the flour until smooth, then stir the slurry and ketchup into the pot and cook about 15 minutes more.
**Finish:** Remove the Scotch bonnet and thyme stems, fold in the butter beans to heat through and scatter the remaining scallions on top. Serve with white rice or rice and peas.

notes: Recipe from Golden Krust Caribbean Bakery and Grill, adapted by Sam Sifton for NYT Cooking.
The same blackened sugar and two-stage aromatic method drives the Jamaican Brown Stew Oxtail practice batch in this book.

sources.label: NYT Cooking (Golden Krust, adapted by Sam Sifton)

recipes.title: Smoked Mackerel Rundown
recipes.description: Melissa Thompson's Jamaican rundown: smoked mackerel cooked down in spiced coconut milk with yam or pumpkin, tomatoes and peppers, served with boiled green bananas.

ingredients.name: Rundown
items: 7 to 8 oz yellow yam or pumpkin, peeled, seeded if needed and chopped
6 smoked mackerel fillets, skin removed, or 2 (3.5- to 5-ounce) tins smoked mackerel, drained
**Onion:** Heat about 1 tbsp oil in a large, deep lidded skillet over medium. Fry the onion, stirring occasionally, until it starts to soften, about 5 minutes.
**Vegetables:** Add the yam, tomatoes, bell pepper, garlic, ginger, pimento, cumin and thyme and cook, stirring occasionally, 5 minutes more.
**Coconut:** Stir in the coconut milk and bay leaves with a splash of water, cover and cook until the yam softens, 15 to 20 minutes.
**Mackerel:** Uncover, stir in the mackerel and cook until the sauce thickens, about 10 minutes. Season with salt if needed.
**Green bananas:** If using, trim the ends and cut each banana into 2 or 3 pieces. Boil in salted water until tender, about 10 minutes, then lift out and peel.
**Serve:** Serve the rundown with the boiled green bananas.

notes: Recipe from Melissa Thompson, adapted by Ligaya Mishan for NYT Cooking.

sources.label: NYT Cooking (Melissa Thompson, adapted by Ligaya Mishan)

recipes.title: Jerk Spiced Duck Tacos (Bon Appétit)
recipes.description: Build-your-own tacos. Low and slow roast renders the fat and makes the meat fall-apart tender.

items: 16 habanero chiles, stems removed (keep the seeds; the duck fat tames the heat)
2 pieces (2 inch) ginger, scrubbed and crushed
**Score:** With a clean razor blade or very sharp thin knife, cut through the skin and fat but not into the flesh. Salt generously. Place each duck in a large resealable bag.
**Marinade:** Finely grind allspice. Add to a blender with finely grated nutmeg, habaneros, soy sauce, rum, vinegar, and sugar. Purée smooth.
**Marinate:** Divide marinade between the bags, add ginger to each. Seal, press out air, work the marinade around. Refrigerate breast side down 12 hours.
**Roast:** About 300 to 325°F for 5 hours. Drain fat every 45 to 60 minutes.

notes: Keep the ducks whole (don't butterfly) so they self-baste.
The roast yields 2+ cups of habanero spiced duck fat. Save it for plantains or potatoes.
Pairs well with pickled onions, cilantro, lime, and a cooling slaw.

extras.title: Timeline from frozen (5pm dinner)
extras.body:
- 3 days before: move ducks from freezer to fridge.
- Night before: score and start the 12 hour marinade.
- Day of: into the oven by about 12pm.

recipes.title: Mexican Style Flank Steak Tacos (Stovetop + Oven)

items: 1 tsp dried oregano (Mexican if you have it)
Whisk everything from olive oil through cilantro into a marinade.
Marinate steak 2 hours minimum, ideally 4 to 8. Max 12 hours.
Rest at room temp 30 minutes. Preheat oven to 400°F. Pat steak dry.
Sear in smoking hot cast iron 2 to 3 minutes per side.
Move skillet to oven 4 to 7 minutes. Pull at 130°F (medium-rare) to 135°F (medium).
Char tortillas over a gas flame 15 to 20 seconds per side. Wrap in a towel.
Slice thin (1/4 inch) against the grain on a slight bias.
Double up tortillas, add steak, onion, cilantro, lime. Salsa on the side.

notes: Deeper flavor: swap soy for 1 tbsp soy plus 1 tsp Worcestershire.
Smokier: add 1 minced chipotle in adobo plus 1 tsp adobo sauce to the marinade.
Extra toppings: pickled red onion, queso fresco, radish, avocado, salsa macha.

recipes.title: Short Rib Bulgogi

items: 2 lb thinly sliced boneless short rib
1/2 cup grated Asian pear (about half a pear)
1/2 yellow onion, grated or thinly sliced
If not pre-sliced, freeze meat 30 to 45 minutes, slice 1/8 inch against the grain. Pat dry.
Whisk everything except green onions into a marinade.
Marinate at least 30 minutes, up to overnight. Not much past 24 hours (the pear turns it mushy).
Sear in batches in a nearly smoking cast iron or grill, 1 to 2 minutes per side. Don't crowd.
Top with green onions and sesame. Serve with rice, lettuce wraps, kimchi, or ssamjang.

notes: Bone-in LA galbi works with the same marinade, just grill a bit longer.

recipes.title: Thai Red Curry with Chicken (Gaeng Daeng Gai)

items: 3 tbsp Thai red curry paste (Mae Ploy or Maesri)
**Crack the coconut cream:** Heat oil, add coconut cream, stir 3 to 4 minutes until it splits and oil separates.
Fry curry paste in it about 2 minutes until fragrant and darker.
Add chicken, cook 3 to 4 minutes until no longer pink outside.
Add coconut milk, bring to a gentle boil. Add lime leaves, fish sauce, sugar. Simmer 10 minutes.
Add bamboo shoots and pepper, cook 3 to 4 minutes.
Off heat, stir in basil, top with chilies. Adjust with fish sauce or sugar. Serve over jasmine rice.

extras.title: Variations
extras.body:
(from the Gaeng Phet version in the Rolodex build chat)
- Beef: flank steak, simmer 15 to 20 minutes.
- Shrimp: add at the end, 3 to 4 minutes.
- Vegetarian: firm tofu, mushroom stock, light soy in place of fish sauce.
- Duck: leftover roast duck added at the end with the basil. Good use for jerk duck leftovers.
- Balance check: more salt, add fish sauce. Too salty or spicy, add sugar. Flat, squeeze of lime.

recipes.title: Thai Green Curry with Chicken (Gaeng Khiao Wan Gai)

items: 150g Thai eggplant, quartered (or Japanese eggplant, cubed)
100g pea eggplant or green beans, trimmed
Crack coconut cream in oil, 3 to 4 minutes until glossy and oil separates.
Fry curry paste 2 minutes. Add chilies, toss briefly.
Add coconut milk, lime leaves, fish sauce, sugar, eggplant. Simmer 10 minutes.
Off heat, stir in basil and lime juice. Adjust seasoning. Serve with jasmine rice or roti.

notes: Red and green share most of the same base, so both can be made together as a dinner spread.

recipes.title: Khao Pad (Thai Fried Rice)

items: 6 oz chicken thigh or shrimp, bite-sized
Break up cold rice by hand. (Fresh rice: spread on a sheet pan, refrigerate uncovered 1 hour.)
Heat wok on highest heat, oil until just smoking.
Sear protein 60 seconds untouched, stir-fry until cooked. Remove.
Garlic and shallot 15 seconds. Push aside, scramble eggs into large curds.
Add rice, press flat, let it char. Toss every 30 seconds for 2 to 3 minutes.
Return protein. Add fish sauce, soy, sugar, white pepper. Toss 30 seconds. Add tomato and scallions, toss briefly.
Serve with lime, cucumber, chilies. Squeeze lime right before eating.

notes: Small batches for wok hei. Golden Mountain seasoning sauce in place of soy for extra authenticity.

items: **Boil chicken** with 1 chopped onion, half the garlic and ginger, thyme, half the curry powder, 1 stock cube, and salt in water to barely cover. Cook through (about 25 minutes). Reserve stock.
**Fry chicken** in half the oil until golden. Set aside.
**Blend** tomatoes, bell peppers, scotch bonnets, remaining onion. Boil to reduce about 15 minutes.
**Fry tomato paste** in remaining oil with remaining garlic and ginger until darkened.

**Build stew:** Add reduced pepper blend, bay leaves, remaining curry powder and stock cubes. Fry on medium, stirring often, until oil rises to the top (20 to 30 minutes). This is the heart of the dish.
**Simmer** with fried chicken and a splash of stock, 10 to 15 minutes.

extras.title: Serve with
extras.body: white rice, jollof, boiled yam, or fried plantain. Freezes well.

items: 2 slices day-old Italian bread, crusts removed
Soak torn bread in milk 5 minutes. Squeeze out excess, keep damp.
Beat egg, add bread, Parm, parsley, garlic, salt, pepper. Add turkey, mix by hand until just combined.
With wet hands, gently roll 1.5 inch balls. Don't pack tight.
**Nonna way:** nestle raw into simmering red sauce, cover, low simmer 25 to 30 minutes without moving much.
**Or:** brown in olive oil 7 to 8 minutes, then finish in sauce 15 minutes.

extras.title: Turkey tips
extras.body: Milk-soaked bread is non-negotiable. Grate in a little fresh onion for juiciness. If using 99% lean breast, add 1 tbsp olive oil to the mix.

recipes.title: Creamy Lemon Pesto Pasta
recipes.description: Kirkland pesto turned silky and clingy (not oily) with pasta water, mascarpone, butter, and lemon.

items: 8 oz short pasta (fusilli, gemelli, or rigatoni)
1 tbsp kosher salt, for pasta water
2 tbsp mascarpone or ricotta (or heavy cream)
1/3 cup grated Parmesan, plus more to serve
1/4 tsp black pepper or red pepper flakes
**Boil:** Salt a large pot of boiling water and cook the pasta until about 1 minute shy of al dente.
**Sauce base:** While it cooks, stir the pesto and mascarpone together in a large bowl. Zest about half the lemon into the bowl.
**Save water and drain:** Scoop out about 1 cup of pasta water, then drain. Don't rinse.
**Emulsify:** Whisk 2 to 3 tbsp hot pasta water into the pesto mixture until smooth, creamy, and pale green.
**Toss:** Add the hot pasta and cold butter. Toss hard for about 30 seconds, adding pasta water a spoonful at a time until glossy and every piece is coated.
**Cheese:** Add the Parmesan and toss again until the sauce thickens and clings.
**Lemon:** Squeeze in 1 to 2 tsp lemon juice, toss, and taste. Adjust juice and salt.
**Serve:** Top with extra zest, Parmesan, and pepper. Serve right away.

notes: Keep the pesto off direct heat the whole time. Heat breaks the emulsion (oily) and dulls the basil.
Pasta water is the key: its starch emulsifies the oil, thickens the sauce, and helps it cling. Use a bit less water in the pot for starchier water.
Juice goes in last so it tastes fresh and doesn't break the cream. Zest carries most of the lemon flavor.
Leftovers tighten in the fridge; loosen with a splash of water or milk when reheating.

recipes.title: Birria de Res (Beef Birria)
recipes.description: Josef Centeno's thickly sauced beef birria, based on his grandmother Alice's recipe: bone-in beef braised in a smoky guajillo and poblano adobo, served in bowls with warm tortillas.

items: 5 guajillo chiles, seeded, stemmed and halved lengthwise
5 pounds bone-in beef shoulder, cut into large pieces (or goat or lamb stew cuts on the bone)
1/4 cup neutral oil, such as canola or grapeseed
1/4 cup plus 2 tbsp distilled white vinegar

**Poblanos:** Char the poblanos directly over a gas flame on high, turning, until blackened all over, about 2 minutes per side. Cover in a bowl to steam 10 minutes, then peel off the skins, remove the stems and seeds, and roughly chop.
**Guajillos:** Meanwhile, toast the guajillo halves flat in a large skillet over medium, in batches, about 15 seconds, turning once. Soak them in 2 cups hot water.

**Sear:** Season the meat all over with the salt. Heat the oil in a large ovenproof pot over medium-high and sear the meat in batches until well browned, 2 to 3 minutes per side. Move to a bowl as you go.
**Onion:** Add the onion to the pot and cook, stirring occasionally, until golden, about 5 minutes. Return all the meat.
**Adobo:** Blend the tomatoes, vinegar, garlic, ginger, oregano, sesame seeds, cumin, cloves and a few grinds of pepper with the poblanos, guajillos and their soaking liquid until smooth.
**Braise:** Pour the adobo over the meat, add the cinnamon stick and bay leaves, and add 4 to 6 cups water, enough to cover the meat well.
**Bake:** Cover and cook in the oven until fork-tender, about 2 hours.
**Serve:** Ladle into bowls, sprinkle with cilantro, and serve with lime wedges and warm tortillas.

notes: Recipe from Josef Centeno, adapted by Tejal Rao for NYT Cooking.
Skim the red fat off the top and save it with leftover meat for the Quesabirria Tacos.
Leftover broth (consomé) makes a great birria ramen with an egg and fresh herbs.
Oxtail, lamb on the bone or even tofu work in place of beef.

sources.label: NYT Cooking (Josef Centeno, adapted by Tejal Rao)

recipes.title: Quesabirria Tacos
recipes.description: Crisp, cheesy tacos made from leftover birria: tortillas dipped in the red, seasoned fat skimmed from the pot, filled with shredded meat and cheese and pan-fried until lacy at the edges.

items: 1/4 cup seasoned birria fat plus 1 cup leftover birria meat (both from Birria de Res)
1 cup shredded low-moisture cheese, such as Monterey Jack
**Prep:** Spoon the red-stained fat off the top of the birria onto a plate. Shred the meat by hand or with a fork; it should be lightly dressed in broth, not swimming in it.

**Fry:** Heat a large nonstick or cast-iron skillet over medium. Working quickly, dip one side of each tortilla in the fat and lay it in the pan, fat side down. As it sizzles, cover each with 1/4 cup cheese all the way to the edges, then scatter about 1/4 cup meat over half.

**Fold:** As the tortillas brown and the cheese melts, fold them over the meat and press gently. Spilled cheese is good; it makes lacy, crisp edges. Flip as needed and cook until crisp on both sides without burning.
**Serve:** Lift the edge of each taco and add onion, cilantro and a squeeze of lime.

notes: By Tejal Rao for NYT Cooking.
Salsa or hot sauce are welcome, but the birria fat carries plenty of flavor on its own.

recipes.title: Stew Peas and Spinners
recipes.description: Jamaican stew peas: red kidney beans simmered with coconut milk and salted pig's tail or beef, finished with thyme, Scotch bonnet and hand-rolled spinner dumplings.

items: 2 pounds salted pig's tail, chopped, or 1 pound beef stew meat (such as chuck), cut into large chunks

**Soak:** Rinse the peas and soak them in a large pot of cold water in the fridge overnight, or at least 8 hours. Rinse the pig's tail, if using, and soak it in cold water in the fridge the same amount of time. (If using beef, salt it right before cooking.)

**Simmer:** Drain the peas, leaving them in the pot, and add the garlic, scallions and drained pig's tail or salted beef. Add water to just cover, bring to a simmer and stir in the coconut milk. Simmer at least 2 1/2 hours, until the meat is fork-tender and the peas are cooked, skimming foam and topping up with water to keep everything covered.
**Season:** Add the chile and thyme and simmer 30 minutes more, seasoning with salt and pepper.

**Spinners:** Meanwhile, stir the flour with a pinch of salt, then stir in 1/4 cup water until a dough forms, adding more water a teaspoon at a time if dry. Roll tablespoon-size pieces between your palms into thin ropes about 5 inches long and a scant 1/2 inch thick. Keep them apart until all the dough is used.
**Finish:** About 15 minutes before serving, stir the spinners into the pot and simmer until cooked through, about 15 minutes. Serve hot with white rice.

notes: By Bryan Washington for NYT Cooking.
Every cook's version differs; adjust garlic, meat, peppers and herbs to taste. Chicken or a vegetarian version work too.

recipes.title: Spicy Red Pesto Pasta
recipes.description: A red pesto inspired by pesto alla Siciliana: toasted sun-dried tomatoes, walnuts, tomato paste and chile blitzed with roasted red peppers and Parmesan, with basil as a garnish.

items: 2/3 cup plus 1 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
1/2 cup drained jarred oil-packed sun-dried tomatoes (about 3 1/2 oz), roughly chopped
1/2 cup coarsely chopped walnuts (a scant 2 1/2 oz)
3 tbsp double-concentrated tomato paste (or 1/3 cup tomato paste)
1/2 cup drained, chopped jarred roasted red peppers (about 4 oz)
1 1/2 oz finely grated Parmesan (about 1 packed cup), plus more for serving
1 pound rigatoni, orecchiette or other shaped pasta
Sliced fresh basil leaves, for serving

**Toast:** Bring a large pot of water to a boil. In a large skillet, heat 1 tbsp of the oil over medium-high. Add the sun-dried tomatoes, walnuts, tomato paste, garlic and red-pepper flakes, season with 1/2 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp pepper, and cook, stirring, until toasted and fragrant, about 5 minutes. Move to a bowl to cool a few minutes.
**Pesto:** Put the roasted peppers and Parmesan in a food processor, top with the cooled tomato mixture and the remaining 2/3 cup oil, and pulse into a paste. It makes about 2 cups.
**Pasta:** Salt the boiling water generously and cook the pasta until al dente. Reserve 1 1/2 cups pasta water, then drain.

**Toss:** Return the pasta to the pot with about 1 1/2 cups pesto and 1 cup pasta water, and stir vigorously until glossy and evenly coated. Add more pesto or pasta water to taste and season with salt and pepper.
**Serve:** Top with Parmesan, torn basil and lemon zest if using. Serve right away.

notes: By Alexa Weibel for NYT Cooking.
Stir in a splash of heavy cream for a richer sauce.
Extra pesto is great on steak, sandwiches, a cheese board or crudités.

recipes.title: Ricotta Pasta Alla Vodka
recipes.description: Spicy, bacon-laced vodka sauce that glossily coats the pasta, finished with three cool dollops of whole-milk ricotta on each plate.

items: 4 slices thick-cut bacon (6 oz), coarsely chopped
4 large garlic cloves, crushed but left whole
3/4 to 1 cup vodka, depending on how boozy you want it
4 oz Pecorino Romano or Parmesan, finely grated (1 cup)
Finely chopped flat-leaf parsley or basil, for serving
**Water:** Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.
**Bacon:** Heat a large, high-sided skillet over medium-high. Cook the oil and bacon, stirring occasionally, until crisp at the edges, about 5 minutes. Pour off all but 3 tbsp fat and save the rest.

**Aromatics:** Lower to medium and stir in the pepper flakes, oregano and garlic for a few seconds until fragrant. Add the onion, season well with salt and pepper and cook over medium-high until translucent, about 5 minutes, adding bacon fat if dry.
**Tomato paste and vodka:** Stir in the tomato paste and cook, stirring constantly, until slightly darker, about 3 minutes. Turn off the heat and stir in the vodka.
**Pasta:** Cook the pasta until 2 minutes shy of al dente.
**Reduce:** Meanwhile, return the sauce to high heat and cook, stirring, until reduced by three-quarters, about 2 minutes. Add the cream, bring to a simmer and take off the heat.

**Toss:** Reserve 2 cups pasta water, then drain. Add the pasta to the sauce with 1 cup pasta water and most of the pecorino. Cook over medium-high, stirring hard and shaking the pan, until the sauce glossily coats the pasta, 5 to 7 minutes, adding more water if dry. Remove the garlic and season to taste.
**Serve:** Plate, sprinkle with the remaining pecorino, add three spoonfuls of ricotta to each serving and top with parsley.

notes: By Eric Kim for NYT Cooking.
The vodka helps the fat emulsify into a glossy, creamy sauce.
The cool ricotta and fresh parsley balance the spicy, boozy sauce.

recipes.title: Pasta Alla Norma Sorta
recipes.description: A loose take on pasta alla Norma: roasted eggplant in a burst cherry tomato sauce with chile, melted mozzarella, crispy prosciutto and fresh herbs.

items: 1 1/2 pounds eggplant, unpeeled, cut into 1/2-inch dice
1/4 cup plus 2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
3 oz prosciutto, roughly chopped into 1- to 1 1/2-inch pieces
1 medium shallot, thinly sliced into rings
1 Fresno or serrano chile, seeded if you like, thinly sliced into rings
1 1/2 pounds Sun Gold, cherry or grape tomatoes
1 (15-ounce) can diced tomatoes with their juices
1 cup roughly chopped fresh herbs, such as basil and mint

**Roast the eggplant:** Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss the eggplant on a large rimmed sheet pan with 1/4 cup oil, season well and spread in one layer. Roast until golden, 25 to 30 minutes, flipping halfway.

**Crisp the prosciutto:** Meanwhile, heat the remaining oil in a deep 12-inch skillet over medium. Cook the prosciutto, stirring, until crisping and browned in spots, 2 to 3 minutes. Drain on paper towels.

**Sauce:** Add the shallot, garlic and chile and cook until soft and fragrant, about 2 minutes. Add the cherry tomatoes and cook, pressing gently to help some burst, 5 to 7 minutes. Stir in the canned tomatoes, season, and simmer while the eggplant finishes, about 15 minutes, adding 1/4 cup pasta water if dry.
**Pasta:** Cook the pasta in well-salted boiling water until al dente. Reserve 1 cup pasta water and drain.
**Combine:** Stir the eggplant into the sauce, add the pasta and toss, adding pasta water as needed. Stir in the mozzarella until it starts to melt.
**Serve:** Top with the crispy prosciutto, herbs and flaky salt if using.

notes: By Colu Henry for NYT Cooking.
Leave out the prosciutto for a vegetarian version.

recipes.title: Grilled Cheese With Apples and Apple Butter
recipes.description: Sharp Cheddar grilled cheese layered with apple butter and buttery sautéed apples, shallot and rosemary, steamed briefly under a lid so the cheese melts as the bread crisps.

items: 5 tbsp unsalted butter, plus more as needed
1 large Granny Smith apple, cored and thinly sliced
1 small shallot, halved and thinly sliced
8 slices country bread, cut 1/2 inch thick
4 oz sharp Cheddar, sliced 1/4 inch thick

**Apples:** Heat a 12-inch skillet over medium-high, add 1 tbsp butter, then the apples, shallot, rosemary and a pinch of salt. Cook, tossing occasionally, until the apples are golden and soft, 8 to 10 minutes, lowering the heat if the shallots start to burn. Set aside on a plate.

**Prep the bread:** Wipe out the pan and set it over medium with 1 tbsp butter (2 tbsp if cooking two sandwiches at once). Spread one side of each bread slice with 1 tbsp apple butter. Top four slices with 1 oz Cheddar each and the other four with the apple mixture. Don't close them yet.

**Grill:** Put one cheese slice and one apple slice in the pan, butter side down (two of each if they fit), drizzle 2 tsp water into the pan and cover. Cook until the cheese melts and the bread is golden and crisp, 5 to 7 minutes, lowering the heat if needed.
**Serve:** Press the halves together, cut and serve right away. Repeat with the rest, adding butter as needed.

notes: By Susan Spungen for NYT Cooking.

recipes.title: Roast Chicken With Maple Butter and Rosemary
recipes.description: A simple skillet-roasted whole chicken basted with rosemary maple butter until glossy and deep golden.

items: 2 to 3 rosemary sprigs, plus 2 1/2 tsp finely chopped rosemary
**Prep:** Heat the oven to 375°F. Pat the chicken dry and season well inside and out. Set it breast side up in a 10-inch cast-iron or ovenproof skillet and stuff the rosemary sprigs into the cavity.

**Maple butter:** Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium-low, add the chopped rosemary and maple syrup, and cook until fragrant and slightly thickened, 1 to 2 minutes. Spoon it all over the chicken; some will pool in the pan, which is fine.
**Roast:** Roast, basting with the pan juices every 15 to 20 minutes, until glossy, golden and 165°F in the thickest part of the thigh, 55 to 60 minutes.
**Rest:** Baste once more if you like and rest 10 minutes before carving. Whisk the pan juices and pass them at the table.

notes: By Colu Henry for NYT Cooking.

recipes.title: Peruvian Roasted Chicken With Spicy Cilantro Sauce
recipes.description: Chicken marinated in garlic, soy, lime and Peruvian aji pastes, roasted at high heat until the skin is golden, and served with a creamy jalapeño, cilantro and feta sauce.

ingredients.name: Chicken
items: 6 garlic cloves, finely grated or minced
1 tbsp aji amarillo paste, or another chile paste such as sriracha or sambal
1 tsp aji panca paste or 1 tsp pasilla chile powder
1 (3 1/2- to 4 1/2-pound) chicken, halved (see notes), or 4 pounds bone-in, skin-on chicken parts

ingredients.name: Spicy cilantro sauce
items: 1 cup cilantro leaves and tender stems
1 1/2 tbsp lime juice, more to taste
2 tsp chopped fresh oregano or basil
3/4 tsp fine sea salt, more to taste
1/2 tbsp aji amarillo or other chile paste
**Marinade:** In a large bowl, whisk the garlic, soy sauce, aji amarillo, lime juice, aji panca, mustard, cumin, pepper and salt.
**Marinate:** Turn the chicken in the marinade to coat, cover and refrigerate at least 2 hours and up to 12.
**Heat:** Heat the oven to 450°F. Pat the chicken dry, set it skin side up on a rimmed baking sheet and drizzle with oil.
**Roast:** Roast until the skin is golden and the chicken is cooked through, 35 to 45 minutes. If using parts, pull the breasts after 25 to 35 minutes. Rest 10 minutes, loosely tented with foil.

**Sauce:** Meanwhile, blend the cilantro, jalapeños, feta, garlic, lime juice, oregano, salt, mustard, aji amarillo, honey and cumin until smooth. With the motor running, drizzle in the oil until emulsified. Adjust the salt and lime.
**Serve:** Carve the chicken and serve with the sauce and lime wedges.

notes: By Melissa Clark for NYT Cooking.
To halve a chicken, cut lengthwise through the breastbone with poultry shears, then turn it over and cut along the backbone. Remove the backbone entirely if you like.

recipes.title: Peruvian Pork Stew With Chiles, Lime and Apples
recipes.description: A largely hands-off stew of browned pork shoulder simmered with onions, apples, ancho chiles, bay and cloves, brightened with lime. Works on the stove or in a slow cooker.

items: 3 to 4 pounds trimmed boneless pork shoulder, cut into 2-inch pieces
4 large apples, peeled, cored and roughly chopped
3 ancho or other mild dried chiles, snipped and seeded

**Brown:** Heat the oil in a skillet and brown the pork on all sides, in batches if needed. Meanwhile, sauté the onions and apples with the chiles, bay leaves and cloves until the onions are tender, about 10 minutes.

**Combine:** Put everything, including the lime juice and stock, in a Dutch oven or slow cooker. Bring to a boil, then adjust to a steady but gentle bubble. (In a slow cooker, set it on high for 4 to 6 hours.)

**Simmer:** Cook, stirring every 30 minutes or so, until the meat is very tender and nearly falling apart, at least 1 hour. Adjust the seasoning, then lower the heat; it holds well for at least an hour.
**Serve:** Lift out the meat and reduce the broth as needed. Serve over steamed rice, topped with cilantro.

notes: By Mark Bittman for NYT Cooking.

recipes.title: Roasted Dumpling Squash with Sage Brown Butter
recipes.description: Sweet dumpling squash has thin, edible skin, so there's no peeling. High-heat roasting caramelizes the edges, then a maple sage brown butter goes on top.

ingredients.name: Squash
items: Pinch of cayenne or chipotle powder
**Heat:** Preheat the oven to 425°F with a rack in the lower third. Line a sheet pan with parchment.
**Cut:** Microwave each whole squash 2 minutes to soften it for cutting. Halve stem to base, scoop out the seeds, and cut into 1 inch wedges along the ridges. Leave the skin on.
**Season:** Toss the wedges with olive oil, salt, pepper, cinnamon and cayenne. Spread out cut side down with space between them.
**Roast:** Roast 15 minutes, flip, then roast 10 to 15 minutes more until tender and deeply browned at the edges.

**Brown butter:** While the squash roasts, melt butter in a small pan over medium. Add sage and cook 2 to 3 minutes until the butter smells nutty and turns golden brown and the sage is crisp. Off heat, stir in maple syrup and vinegar.
**Finish:** Spoon the brown butter and crispy sage over the hot squash. Top with pepitas, flaky salt and cheese if using.

notes: Halves instead of wedges: roast cut side down 30 to 35 minutes, then fill with the brown butter, or stuff with wild rice, sausage or quinoa.
Delicata, carnival or acorn squash all work. Acorn skin is tougher, so add 5 to 10 minutes.
Roast the seeds: rinse, dry, toss with oil and salt, and bake at 325°F for 15 to 20 minutes.
Miso swap: whisk 1 tsp white miso into the brown butter instead of the vinegar.
Good next to the jerk duck tacos, or on the Thanksgiving table.

recipes.title: Split Pea Soup
recipes.description: A customizable split pea soup: smoky with bacon or ham hock, or vegetarian with smoked paprika. Adding the peas in two batches gives every spoonful some texture.

items: 6 slices bacon, or 1 (1-pound) smoked ham hock, or 1 tsp smoked paprika
2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, plus more as needed
2 medium leeks, white and pale green parts, rinsed and thinly sliced (about 1 3/4 cups)
2 medium carrots, scrubbed and diced (about 1 1/2 cups)
1 pound dried split green peas, divided
8 to 12 cups chicken stock or water

**Start the base:** With bacon, cook it in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium until crisp, 12 to 13 minutes, then set it aside to crumble later and keep the fat in the pot. With a ham hock, heat the oil over medium-high and brown the hock until golden, about 6 minutes. For vegetarian, just heat the oil over medium.
**Vegetables:** Add the leeks, garlic and onion, season well with salt and pepper, and cook over medium, stirring, until tender, 5 to 8 minutes. Add a little oil if they look dry.

**First simmer:** Stir in the carrots, paprika (if using), half the split peas, the thyme and 8 cups stock or water. Bring to a boil, then simmer partly covered, stirring now and then, until the peas are tender, about 45 minutes.
**Mash:** Coarsely mash with a potato masher or a few pulses of an immersion blender, watching for the thyme sprigs. Blend longer for a smoother soup.
**Second simmer:** Add the remaining split peas and simmer until soft, about 1 hour. Add stock or water if it gets too thick, or simmer uncovered to thicken.
**Finish:** If using a ham hock, pull the meat off the bone, cube it and stir it in. Season with salt and pepper and serve with crumbled bacon and lemon wedges.

notes: By Ali Slagle for NYT Cooking.
Make up to 1 week ahead. Add stock when reheating if it has thickened.

recipes.title: Butternut Squash Congee With Chile Oil
recipes.description: A seasonal congee made quickly from leftover rice. Butternut squash melts into a creamy, golden porridge, finished with scallions and chile oil.

items: 2 tightly packed cups leftover medium- or long-grain rice, preferably refrigerated
1 tbsp neutral oil, such as canola
1 tsp kosher salt (such as Diamond Crystal), plus more to taste
1 pound butternut squash (about 1/2 small), peeled, seeded and cut into 1-inch pieces
Chile oil or chile crisp, for serving
**Combine:** In a large pot, stir together the rice, oil and salt, breaking up any clumps. Add the stock, garlic, squash and kombu (if using) and bring to a boil over medium-high.
**Simmer:** Reduce the heat to low, cover and simmer 30 minutes.
**Break down:** Uncover, stir, raise the heat to medium and simmer 5 to 10 minutes more, until the rice has broken down.

**Stir:** Turn off the heat and remove any large pieces of kombu (leaving some is fine). Stir vigorously with a wooden spoon to break up the rice, squash and garlic. Some squash stays in pieces; the rest turns the congee golden. Salt to taste.
**Serve:** Top with scallions and a few drops of chile oil or chile crisp.

notes: By Hetty Lui McKinnon for NYT Cooking.
The vigorous final stir is what makes it creamy.
Easier squash prep: cut it into smaller pieces before peeling, or buy pre-cut cubes.

recipes.title: Red Peas Soup
recipes.description: Hearty Jamaican red kidney bean soup with smoked turkey, coconut milk and optional dumplings. It's thick and spicy enough to pass as a stew.

ingredients.name: Soup
items: 8 cups water or low-sodium chicken stock
1 (1.75-ounce) package cock-flavored soup mix, such as Grace
1 medium sweet potato or yam, diced
**Soak:** Cover the beans with 4 to 6 cups water in a large bowl and soak overnight.

**Turkey:** Put the smoked turkey in a large, heavy pot with enough water or stock to cover (about 8 cups). Boil over medium 30 minutes, skimming off the foam. Drain the beans and add them to the pot.

**Simmer:** Add the coconut milk, soup mix, garlic, scallions, thyme, onion, Scotch bonnet, bouillon, allspice and black pepper. Simmer over medium until the beans are tender, 1 to 2 hours, adding water as needed.
**Dumplings:** If using, mix the flour and salt, then stir in 1 cup water until shaggy and wet.

**Vegetables:** Lift out the turkey, pull the meat from the bones and return it to the pot. Add the sweet potato and carrot, drop in spoonfuls of dumpling dough, and cook over medium, flipping the dumplings once or twice, until everything is tender, about 15 minutes.
**Finish:** Discard the thyme, Scotch bonnet and scallions. Adjust the seasoning, thin with water if it's too thick, and serve hot, over rice if you like.

notes: By Millie Peartree for NYT Cooking.
Smoked turkey necks stand in for the salted pig tails some versions use; either brings deep smokiness.
Look for cock-flavored soup mix in the international aisle.

recipes.title: Soup Joumou
recipes.description: Haitian squash soup with epis-marinated beef, vegetables, vermicelli and dumplings. Haitians traditionally eat it on Jan. 1 to celebrate independence.

ingredients.name: Epis seasoning
items: 1 large green bell pepper, stemmed and chopped
1 medium red bell pepper, stemmed and chopped
1/2 tsp fresh or dried thyme leaves

ingredients.name: Soup
items: 1 pound boneless beef chuck, cut into 1/2-inch pieces
1/2 cup fresh lime juice (from about 3 limes)
2 pounds calabaza squash, peeled and roughly chopped
5 medium Idaho or russet potatoes, peeled and cut into 3/4-inch cubes
1/2 small head green cabbage, shredded (about 3 cups)
1/4 tsp fresh or dried thyme leaves
**Epis:** Purée all the epis ingredients in a blender. Use now or refrigerate in a jar up to 6 weeks.
**Marinate:** Rinse the beef in lukewarm water, then rub it all over with the lime juice. Toss with 5 tbsp epis, cover and refrigerate at least 30 minutes, ideally overnight.
**Squash:** Purée the calabaza with 1 cup water in a blender and set aside.

**Brown:** Heat the oil in a large pot over medium. Add the beef with its marinade, the tomato paste and the bouillon cube, crumbled. Cook, stirring occasionally, until it caramelizes and darkens, about 10 minutes. Move the meat to a bowl.

**Build the soup:** Add 6 cups water to the pot and bring to a boil over high. Stir in the squash purée, potatoes, cabbage, carrots, onion, celery, scallions, parsley, Scotch bonnet, thyme, salt and pepper and return to a boil. Stir in the beef and its juices.
**Simmer:** Once boiling, cover, reduce to low and simmer 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
**Vermicelli:** Carefully remove the Scotch bonnet without letting it burst. Stir in the vermicelli and cook 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.

**Dumplings:** Meanwhile, stir the flour, oil, salt, pepper and 1/2 cup water into a dough, kneading lightly if needed. Roll 1-tablespoon pieces between your palms into logs about 4 inches long and drop them into the soup as you go. Cook on low, stirring now and then, until cooked through but still firm, 15 to 20 minutes.
**Serve:** Thin with about 1 cup water if you like, then serve warm.

notes: From Cindy Similien's "Let's Speak Haitian Food," adapted by Priya Krishna for NYT Cooking.
Leftover epis keeps 6 weeks and works like sofrito: marinate beef, fish or chicken, or stir it into rice and soups.
If the Scotch bonnet bursts, the soup gets very spicy.

sources.label: NYT Cooking (Cindy Similien, adapted by Priya Krishna)

recipes.title: Sancocho
recipes.description: Von Diaz's Puerto Rican sancocho: a thick, hearty stew of pork and chicken with sofrito, yuca, yautia, plantains, calabaza, corn and chorizo.

items: 1 pound pork or beef stew meat, trimmed and cut into 2-inch pieces
1 pound boneless chicken thighs, trimmed and cut into 2-inch pieces
1 1/2 tbsp kosher salt (such as Diamond Crystal), plus more to taste
1 tbsp olive oil, plus more as needed
Fresh bread or white rice, for serving

**Prep the vegetables:** Peel the yuca, yautia and both plantains and cut into 1-inch pieces. Seed the calabaza and cut it into 1-inch pieces with the skin on. Keep each in its own bowl of water so they don't brown.
**Corn:** Husk the corn and slice into 2-inch segments.
**Season:** Season the pork and chicken with 1/2 tbsp salt and the pepper.

**Brown:** Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large pot over medium-high. Brown the pork on all sides, 5 minutes, and move to a bowl. Brown the chicken on both sides, another 5 minutes, adding oil if needed, and add it to the bowl.
**Sofrito:** Lower the heat to medium, add the sofrito and scrape up the browned bits. Cook until the liquid evaporates and it darkens, 5 to 7 minutes.

**Simmer:** Return the meat and juices to the pot with the stock, bay leaves and remaining 1 tbsp salt. Bring to a boil over high, then simmer uncovered over medium-low 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
