**Vegetables in order:** Drain the vegetables and add them from firmest to softest, 5 minutes apart: yuca, yautia, green plantain, yellow plantain, calabaza, then corn. The yuca gets about 30 minutes total and the corn just 5.

**Chorizo:** Stir in the chorizo and cook 10 to 15 minutes more over medium-low, until the meat and vegetables are fork-tender. Some vegetables will break down and thicken it like porridge, which is what you want.
**Serve:** Adjust the salt and serve with fresh bread or white rice.

notes: By Von Diaz for NYT Cooking.
Look for yuca and yautia at Hispanic, Caribbean or Asian markets or in the freezer section. Potatoes can sub in with less cooking time.
Nearly everything can be swapped, and it makes a hearty vegetarian stew without the meat.

recipes.title: Best Black Bean Soup
recipes.description: Big-tasting, meat-free black bean soup with chipotle, red wine and Mexican oregano. Season generously and purée sparingly, so whole beans swim in a velvety broth, then add quick-pickled onions and garnishes.

ingredients.name: Soup
items: 1 small (7-ounce) can chipotle chiles in adobo (see notes)
2 quarts mild vegetable or chicken stock

ingredients.name: Pickled onions and garnishes
items: 1 small red onion, peeled and thinly sliced
**Chipotle purée:** Purée the whole can of chipotles until smooth and set aside. Put a kettle of water on to boil and keep it hot.
**Vegetables:** In a large, heavy pot, heat the oil over medium until shimmering. Cook the carrots, onions and garlic, stirring, until softened but not browned, 5 to 8 minutes.

**Wine:** Add the wine and simmer until the pan is almost dry. Add the jalapeños and cook 2 minutes. Push the vegetables aside, fry 2 tsp chipotle purée in the center for a minute, then stir it all together.

**Beans:** Add the beans, stock, oregano and bay leaves. Boil 10 to 15 minutes, then simmer partly covered, stirring occasionally and adding hot water to keep it loose and runny, until the beans are just soft, 1 to 2 hours. Add the salt and pepper and keep cooking until the beans are fully soft.
**Pickled onions:** Meanwhile, toss the onion with the lime juice and a sprinkle of salt and let sit until crunchy and tart, about 30 minutes. Drain, rinse in cold water, squeeze dry and refrigerate.
**Texture:** You want whole beans, soft chunks and a velvety broth. If it's thin, purée a small amount of beans and stir them back in, repeating until it's right. It thickens as it sits.
**Season:** Heat through and adjust with salt, pepper, drops of red wine vinegar and dabs of chipotle purée.
**Serve:** Ladle into deep bowls and garnish with sour cream, pickled onions, cilantro, sliced chiles and avocado.

notes: By Julia Moskin for NYT Cooking.
No chipotles? Use 1 tbsp each ground cumin and ground coriander, added with the jalapeños.
If your tap water is hard, add the wine with the stock instead (acid can keep beans from softening), or use distilled water.

recipes.title: Coconut Black Bean Soup
recipes.description: A quick, creamy black bean soup made with canned beans and coconut milk, half-blended for body and brightened with lime, cilantro and quick-pickled onion.

items: 2 limes, 1 halved and 1 cut into wedges
1 3/4 tsp kosher salt (Diamond Crystal, or 3/4 tsp Morton), plus more to taste
1 jalapeño, seeded if desired and minced
1 bunch cilantro, stems and leaves separated
1 cup vegetable or chicken stock, plus more if needed
**Pickled onion:** Quarter the onion lengthwise. Thinly slice one quarter and toss with the juice of 1/2 lime and 1/4 tsp salt; set aside for serving. Dice the rest.
**Soften:** Heat a large soup pot or Dutch oven over medium-high, add the oil, and cook the diced onion until tender and golden at the edges, 3 to 5 minutes. Stir in the garlic and cook 1 minute.

**Aromatics:** Add the jalapeño and 1/4 cup minced cilantro stems and cook until tender, about 2 minutes. Stir in the tomato paste, cumin seeds, pepper and remaining 1 1/2 tsp salt and cook until the paste darkens, 1 to 2 minutes.
**Simmer:** Add the beans, coconut milk and stock. Bring to a boil, then simmer until thick, 15 to 20 minutes.
**Blend:** Purée with an immersion blender or blender until half-smooth and still a little chunky. Add stock for a brothier soup.
**Finish:** Stir in the juice of the remaining lime half and 1/2 cup chopped cilantro leaves. Adjust salt and lime. Serve topped with the pickled onions and more cilantro, with lime wedges alongside.

notes: By Melissa Clark for NYT Cooking.

recipes.title: Lemony White Bean Soup With Turkey and Greens
recipes.description: A brothy, bright one-pot soup of ground turkey, white beans and sturdy greens with cumin, ginger and a generous finish of herbs and lemon.

items: 1 bunch sturdy greens, such as kale, broccoli rabe, mustard greens or collards
3/4 tsp ground cumin, plus more to taste
1/8 tsp red-pepper flakes, plus more to taste
1 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
2 (15-ounce) cans white beans, drained and rinsed
1 cup chopped soft herbs, such as parsley, mint, dill, basil, tarragon or chives
**Soften:** Heat a large pot over medium-high about 1 minute, add the oil and heat 30 seconds. Sauté the onion and carrot until very soft and browned at the edges, 7 to 10 minutes.
**Greens prep:** Meanwhile, rinse the greens, strip the leaves from the stems and tear into bite-size pieces.

**Turkey:** Add the tomato paste, cumin and pepper flakes and cook until the paste darkens, about 1 minute. Add the turkey, garlic, ginger and salt and cook, breaking up the meat, until browned in spots, 4 to 7 minutes.
**Simmer:** Add the stock and beans and simmer until thick and flavorful, 15 to 25 minutes. Smash some beans for a thicker broth, or leave them whole.
**Greens:** Add the greens and simmer until very soft, 5 to 10 minutes (up to 15 for collards), adding water if it reduces too much.
**Finish:** Stir in the herbs and lemon juice and adjust the salt, cumin and lemon until bright. Serve with a drizzle of olive oil and more pepper flakes.

notes: By Melissa Clark for NYT Cooking.

recipes.title: Citrusy Lentil and Sweet Potato Soup
recipes.description: A fast, bright lentil soup with sweet potato and chard, topped with chard stems quick-pickled in lemon or lime juice with jalapeño.

items: 1 tsp ground cumin or coriander (or a mix)
1 bay leaf, thyme or oregano sprig (optional)
1 jalapeño, halved lengthwise, seeds removed if desired
1 medium sweet potato (8 to 10 oz), peeled and cut into 1/2-inch pieces
1/4 cup lemon or lime juice (from 2 lemons or limes)

**Bloom:** In a large Dutch oven, combine the oil, scallions, garlic, cumin, bay leaf (if using), a pinch of salt and one jalapeño half. Cook over medium, stirring constantly, until softened and fragrant but not browned, 2 to 4 minutes.
**Simmer:** Add 5 cups water, the sweet potato, lentils and 1 1/2 tsp salt. Bring to a simmer over medium-high, then cover and simmer on low 10 minutes.

**Chard topping:** Meanwhile, thinly slice the chard stems up to the leaves and toss them with the citrus juice and a pinch of salt. Thinly slice the other jalapeño half and add as much as you like. Coarsely chop the chard leaves.

**Greens:** Taste the broth; add salt if muted and remove the jalapeño if it's getting too spicy. Stir in the chard leaves, cover and cook until the lentils and sweet potato are tender, 8 to 12 minutes. Thin with water if needed and discard the bay leaf and jalapeño half.
**Serve:** Ladle into bowls and top each with a spoonful of the citrusy chard stems, adding more for a brighter soup.

notes: By Ali Slagle for NYT Cooking.
Soup and topping keep separately up to 3 days. Reheat the soup with a little water and salt, then add the topping.

recipes.title: Pumpkin Soup
recipes.description: Velvety pumpkin soup built on rosemary-caramelized onions, maple and apple cider, warmed with curry powder and nutmeg, and topped with fried sage.

ingredients.name: Soup
items: 2 medium yellow onions, halved and thinly sliced
2 tbsp coarsely chopped fresh rosemary (or 2 tsp dried)
1/2 cup fresh apple cider (or 3/4 cup apple juice)
4 cups low-sodium chicken or vegetable broth, plus more as needed
2 (15-ounce) cans pumpkin purée (not pie filling), or 3 cups homemade purée (see notes)
1/2 tsp ground nutmeg, plus more for serving
1 1/2 tsp kosher salt, plus more as needed
1/2 tsp black pepper, plus more as needed
1/3 cup heavy cream, plus more for serving

**Caramelize:** Melt the butter in a large Dutch oven over medium. Cook the onions and rosemary, stirring occasionally, until lightly caramelized, 15 to 20 minutes, lowering the heat if they brown too fast.
**Deglaze:** Add the maple syrup and garlic and cook until the onions darken, 3 to 5 minutes. Add the cider, scrape up the bits and reduce by about half.
**Simmer:** Add the broth, pumpkin, curry powder, nutmeg, cloves, salt and pepper and bring to a boil. Simmer briskly on medium-low 10 minutes, scraping the bottom so it doesn't scorch.
**Blend:** Purée in batches (or with an immersion blender), return to a simmer, then turn off the heat and stir in the cream. Season and thin with broth if needed.
**Fried sage:** If using, melt the butter in a skillet over medium-high and fry the sage until just crisp, 1 to 2 minutes. Drain on paper towels and keep the butter.
**Serve:** Top each bowl with 2 fried sage leaves and a drizzle of the sage butter, or a swirl of cream and a pinch of nutmeg.

notes: By Lidey Heuck for NYT Cooking.
Homemade purée: roast 1 1/2-inch wedges of a 4- to 5-pound sugar pumpkin, oiled and salted, at 425°F for 35 to 40 minutes, flipping halfway, until very tender. Scoop and mash.
Roast the rinsed seeds with olive oil and salt at 375°F for 10 to 15 minutes.

recipes.title: Thomas Keller's Butternut Squash Soup With Brown Butter
recipes.description: Silky, restaurant-style squash soup built from roasted and simmered squash, strained smooth, then finished with hazelnut brown butter, nutmeg crème fraîche and chives.

items: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
6 cups vegetable stock, more if needed
Bouquet garni: 8 sprigs thyme, 2 sprigs Italian parsley, 2 bay leaves and 1/2 tsp black peppercorns wrapped in 2 green leek leaves

**Roast the bulb:** Heat the oven to 350°F and line a small baking sheet with foil. Cut the neck off the squash and set it aside. Halve the bulb, scoop out the seeds, brush each half inside and out with about 1 1/2 tsp of the oil, season the cavities and tuck in a sage sprig. Roast cut side down until completely tender, about 1 hour. Cool, then scoop out the flesh (discard the sage).
**Dice the neck:** Meanwhile, peel the neck down to the bright orange flesh and cut it into 1/2-inch pieces (about 4 cups).

**Sweat:** Heat the remaining oil in a stockpot over medium-high and cook the leeks, carrots, shallots and onions, stirring often, about 6 minutes. Add the diced squash, garlic, 1 1/2 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp pepper and cook gently 3 minutes without browning. Stir in the honey and cook 2 to 3 minutes.
**Simmer:** Add the stock and bouquet garni, bring to a simmer and cook until the squash is tender, 10 to 15 minutes.

**Blend:** Add the roasted squash and simmer gently about 30 minutes. Discard the bouquet garni, purée in batches, strain through a fine sieve and adjust the seasoning. Cool and refrigerate until serving.
**Crème fraîche:** Whisk the crème fraîche with nutmeg to taste in a chilled bowl until it holds a shape. Cover and refrigerate.

**Brown butter:** Gently reheat the soup, thinning with stock if needed. Heat a medium skillet over high until very hot, add the butter and swirl until hazelnut brown, then pour it into the soup (stand back, it sputters) and stir.
**Serve:** Ladle into 6 bowls and top each with a dollop of crème fraîche, black pepper, chives and a drizzle of olive oil.

notes: Thomas Keller's recipe, by Amanda Hesser for NYT Cooking.
The soup can be made ahead and chilled; add the brown butter just before serving.

recipes.title: Sherried Lentil Soup With Sausage and Croutons
recipes.description: A rustic, partly puréed French lentil soup finished with amontillado sherry and topped with crisp croutons and browned kielbasa.

items: 2 thick slices whole wheat bread, crusts removed, diced

**Lentils:** Heat 3 tbsp oil in a heavy soup pot. Cook the onion, carrot, celery and garlic over low heat until soft. Stir in the thyme and plenty of pepper, add the lentils and 8 cups stock, and simmer until tender, about 45 minutes.

**Topping:** Meanwhile, heat the remaining oil in a skillet and sauté the bread over medium until lightly browned and crisp. Remove to a bowl. Brown the kielbasa in the same pan, add it to the croutons with the parsley and toss.
**Finish:** Purée the lentils in batches in a food processor, keeping some texture. Return to the pot and reheat, adding 1 cup or more stock if too thick. Season with salt and stir in the sherry.
**Serve:** Top each bowl with the kielbasa and croutons.

notes: By Florence Fabricant for NYT Cooking.

recipes.title: Nonna's Sunday Sugo (2 Can Version)
recipes.yield: Makes enough for about 1.5 lb pasta

items: 2 (28 oz) cans San Marzano whole peeled tomatoes (DOP)
Hand crush tomatoes into a bowl.
Olive oil over medium-low. Cook onion with a pinch of salt 8 to 10 minutes until soft (don't brown). Add garlic and pepper flakes 1 minute.
Deglaze with red wine, reduce until mostly evaporated.
Add tomatoes plus 1/3 can of water, oregano, half the basil, Parm rind, salt.
Gentle simmer, then lowest heat, lid cracked. Cook 2 hours minimum, stirring every 20 minutes.
Remove rind, stir in remaining basil. Meatballs go in for the last 45 to 60 minutes.
Serve over rigatoni or spaghetti with Pecorino Romano.

extras.title: Making it a day early
extras.body: Cool uncovered 30 minutes, then refrigerate. Reheat low with a splash of water. Hold the final basil until reheating.

recipes.title: Ponzu Sauce

items: 120ml fresh citrus juice (yuzu, or half lemon half lime)
Simmer mirin 30 seconds to cook off alcohol. Cool.
In a jar combine soy, vinegar, mirin, kombu, bonito. No citrus yet.
Refrigerate 24 hours (4 hours in a pinch).
Strain, pressing the bonito. Stir in citrus juice.
Rest 1 hour before using. Adjust to taste.

notes: Keeps 2 to 3 months refrigerated. Great with shabu-shabu, gyoza, sashimi, salads, grilled fish. Same-day shortcut: whisk soy, citrus, mirin, vinegar, and a pinch of dashi powder.

recipes.title: Pumpkin Pie Spice Blend (No Cardamom)

items: Store airtight in a cool, dark cabinet.

notes: Freshly grated nutmeg is the best upgrade. Potency fades after about 6 months. For a warmer, less sharp blend, cut cloves to 1 tsp and bump cinnamon to 3.5 tbsp.

recipes.title: Kimchi

items: 1 tsp sugar (or rice flour porridge: 1 tbsp rice flour cooked briefly in 1/2 cup water)
**Salt:** Cut cabbage into bite-size pieces. Toss with salt, rest 1 to 2 hours, tossing occasionally. Rinse 2 to 3 times, drain well.
**Paste:** Mix gochugaru, fish sauce, shrimp paste, garlic, ginger, sugar or porridge.
**Combine:** Wearing gloves, massage paste into cabbage, scallions, daikon, carrot.
**Pack:** Press tightly into a clean jar, submerged in its own liquid, 1 inch headspace. Seal loosely.
**Ferment:** Room temp 1 to 3 days, pressing down once or twice daily. Refrigerate once tangy enough.

notes: Use real gochugaru; generic chili flakes won't give the right flavor or color. The rice flour porridge feeds the bacteria for a stronger ferment. Flavor keeps developing in the fridge for weeks.
